title: Qt: Add resolved button to Edit Columns
description:
Add the ability to set custom columns as resolved/unresolved via
the Edit Column frame, if the column fields support it.

Related to #15394.

notes.body: assigned to @johnthacker

Example image:

![image](/uploads/49fcf06521d60c602198abddf65b3bf8/image.png)
Identation seems to be off
Looks like some tabs slipped in there.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/7291/diffs?diff_id=427414799&start_sha=5b4878839d2f78496fab55d6f1326f2437a67830#314b4d8aaa0dd54b69ac397d81ee774f2cacb5cd_122_122)

Everywhere else "saved_resolved_" is being used, just here the direct value from the checkbox is used. to be clear, I would prefer getting rid of "saved_resolved_" but it should be at least consistent.

This is the same as the other options that only apply to COL_CUSTOM and not other types (fields and occurrence), and done for the same reasons.

The `saved_` parameters are the "last value chosen for a column for which it is applicable (i.e. custom column)" so that the control value can be cleared/hidden/disabled if the type is switched to a non custom column where they don't apply, but restored to the last chosen `saved_` parameters if the type is switched back to a custom column.

However, since there is a check for `COL_CUSTOM` there, you're right, we can just use the `saved_` value for (Edit: ) resolved. For occurrence and fields we could call the type conversions on the `saved_` QStrings directly.

My point mainly was, that it was inconsistent that you use the variable throughout, but here the direct value is used.

Btw, in C++ we usually don't use the _ naming convention but camelCase.
I made it simpler, how about this?
Yes, that was what I had in mind
Should we null-check cap_file_ here?
Not needed, because [resolve_column](ui/packet_list_utils.c#L83) has a null check and returns FALSE on null.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/7291/diffs?diff_id=428471753&start_sha=1878128c58ab23c297f298a18aad45c2874e07a5#314b4d8aaa0dd54b69ac397d81ee774f2cacb5cd_96_92)

What is missing is the implementation in Preferences->Appearance->Column. Without that, the user may come into a situation, where he changes it on one side and cannot change it on the other, or worse, opening the preference dialog may cause invalid data issues.

Yes, I definitely mean to add that part (that's #15394). I don't think it leads to invalid data issues, because the resolved parameter always exists, and any such invalid data issues already can be caused by using the right-click context menu of a column. (Or by editing the preferences file directly, but that's at a user's own risk anyway.)

My original thought was to do that in another MR, but I can add that to this one.

Yeah, I did some further investigation you are correct, it wouldn't matter. But it makes sense to add the functionality yet still as it would otherwise be confusing to users. Not sure, if the direct approach is used by the majority of users.
Let's fix that in another MR

I do have one issue after that. The name "Resolve name" is very close to the other "Resolve xxx address" strings. But if you disable name resolution, you still have this column resolve the name. I can see how this may lead to confusion for the user, but currently I do not have a better name myself.

Maybe "Use display value" or "Represent as value/string" would be better? It might make sense to allow the user a choice on how the value is represented via Combobox. Aka: "Display as ... " and then "String/Value"

I would not disable the combobox/checkbox, but hide it where it is not applicable. That way it does not feel like the user cannot do something because he forgot it, but rather because the field does not support it. Also, a tooltip stating to that effect may be a good idea.

I agree with most all of this, but this MR duplicates the behavior in the context menu with the same controls in `packet_list_header.cpp`, which is also a checkbox.

I agree that "Resolve Names" is confusing, but it is the same text as in the context menu for the same option.
Hiding the checkbox makes sense, but the context menu also disables the same checkbox instead of not adding / hiding it.

Adding more to the tooltip (and a tooltip to the context menu in `packet_list_header.cpp`) makes sense.

If I change these things, I would want to change them in the context menu as well, and that starts to look like a different MR (but I suppose it could be combined with this.)
I forgot that we had it in the context menu as well. I think it suffices, that we adapt the tooltip now. We can think about the naming later.
